review_notes:
I read the whole file. It has a small helper namespace (`ReduceEX4`: `stab`, `mem_stab_iff`, `orbitZ`, `mem_orbitZ_iff`, `reps`, `reps_spec`, `countable_GL2`, `countable_quot`) and one very large theorem `solution`.

- The only simp-style candidates are `mem_stab_iff` and `mem_orbitZ_iff`. Both are `Iff.rfl` unfoldings and carry no `@[simp]`. I found no simp call in the file that would use them. They are passed explicitly as hypotheses (`mem_orbitZ_iff σ t`, `mem_stab_iff σ t`) to the imported theorems. I grepped for their other uses and saw only explicit-argument uses in sibling `Sol` files. Marking them `@[simp]` would unfold membership in a structure-defined subgroup and would not clearly improve any use, so I don't recommend it.
- The simp calls in the file are `simp [Subgroup.mem_center_iff]`, `simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]` and `simp_rw [hzero, mul_zero, integral_zero]`. Each is local, targeted and terminating, and none shows a cycle or a competing-rule problem.
- The `attribute [-simp]` and `attribute [-instance]` lines at the top are environment hygiene that comes with the file. I could not tie them to a concrete simp-interface defect in this file.

I did not look further for simp rules in the imported theorem files, and I ran no Lean. So I can't rule out issues that would only show up in other files.
